name: a bent rusty metal sheet, broken concrete lumps, glass shards and a torn cable lying on an oil-stained patch of earth
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-c

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: rusty sheet, concrete lumps, glass shards and cable debris clusters (three groups)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64x48 rectangle of speckled earth with a uniform width of 64 on every row. It has no front face, no eave line and no vertical south face. The earth is seen from straight above. Three small debris clusters (rust-red sheet, grey-white concrete and glass, dark cable) lie on the ground, and the earth texture shows only noise with a dark oil stain near rows 7-10. This is a flat ground decal with no front face, so it reads as a top-down slab, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are acceptable. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 2%, and only 3% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown or rust and read as dark_material_tone. By eye the piece is still shallow. The earth is a mid-brown base with sparse speckles and about 4 lightness steps, where Beodeul materials use 5-6 with per-clump or per-stone shading. The debris (metal sheet, concrete, glass, cable) is a few tiny near-identical clusters of 3-4 tones, repeated across the patch like stamped stickers. The oil stain is barely visible, and there is no tuft, grain or crack structure tying the debris to the soil. Overall it looks thinner and less crafted than the paving reference, with large stretches of plain speckled brown. When in doubt, fail.
